holding_summary: A landlord sued a married-woman tenant for unpaid rent on a three-year lease of two New Orleans residences. The court held her Missouri domicile gave her capacity to contract and be sued as a feme sole without her husband joined, and affirmed judgment for the rent with recognition of the landlord's lien on the leased property. The case treats the residential lease itself as an ordinary, valid, enforceable contract; the actual dispute concerns the tenant's capacity/domicile, not the character of the letting.

holding_summary: Plaintiff leased a room opening onto a gallery from defendant; the gallery railing gave way while plaintiff was moving out, injuring him. The court held a lessor is as much bound to keep the necessary approaches to leased rooms/apartments safe for ordinary use as the apartments themselves, but ultimately found the tenant's own misuse of the railing (lowering furniture over it) was not the ordinary use the lessor warranted, and reversed the judgment for plaintiff.

quotes.text: The lessor, we think, is as much bound for the safety, for ordinary use, of the necessary approaches and exits to and from the apartments which he lets as for the safety of the apartments themselves.
